t: Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid
o: A 3×3 grid holds 9 stones total; move stones between side-adjacent cells (one step per move) until every cell has exactly 1. Cells with >1 stone are sources (with count−1 excess stones), zero cells are sinks; match excess stones to sinks minimizing total Manhattan distance. Example 2: sources (0,1)×2 and (2,2)×2 fill holes (0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(2,1) with cost 4.
k: Only excess stones (grid[i][j]−1 copies) and empty cells matter; their counts are equal.
Cost of assigning a stone to a hole is the Manhattan distance (moves along a grid path, and paths never conflict-increase the total).
Tiny size: try all matchings via permutations, or bitmask DP over hole subsets.

a.i: Collect excess-stone copies and empty cells; since both lists have equal length (≤ 8), enumerate all bijections and take the minimum total Manhattan distance. Correct because any solution induces such a matching and each matched pair costs at least its Manhattan distance, achievable independently.
s: Build extras (repeated per excess stone) and holes lists.
Iterate all permutations of extras zipped with holes; minimize summed Manhattan distances.
a.t: O(p! · h) — p ≤ 8 excess stones, h ≤ 8 holes; trivially fast at this size

a.i: dp[mask] = minimum cost to fill the hole subset mask using the first |mask| excess stones. Transition: assign stone |mask| to any unfilled hole h. This is O(2^h · h) and generalizes beyond 3×3.
s: dp[0] = 0; iterate masks in increasing order.
For each mask, let i = popcount(mask); for each hole h not in mask, relax dp[mask | 1<<h] with dp[mask] + dist(extras[i], holes[h]).
a.t: O(2^h · h) — h ≤ 8, so at most a few thousand states

w: Both approaches are instant at this scale; permutations are easier to write, bitmask DP scales better and shows algorithmic maturity. Key justification to voice: Manhattan distance is a valid lower bound per stone and achievable since intermediate cells can hold any number of stones temporarily. Pitfall: forgetting duplicate excess stones (a cell with 3 stones contributes 2 extras). Follow-up: 4-connected vs 8-connected movement (Chebyshev distance), or larger grids needing Hungarian algorithm.
